reasoning: Both sets are rigorous: walk-forward or known-answer designs, point-in-time readers, per-window PCA instead of copying RF-01's full-sample fit, and every claim sent through the null-hypothesis-testing skill. Set A covers all four stages as specified. That includes PPO agents with a configuration budget and a stop rule, an occasional rented GPU with verified teardown, a hypothesis ledger, a lockbox and a verdict. Its M1 has 27 synthetic golden cases with known answers, and its dependency graph is clean: every spine depends only on the interface task. Set A also has gaps. It drops the user's yahooquery cross-check and their list of 10 delisted names, adds EDGAR, FRED and an unrequested `dataviz` skill, and its packets cite a CONSTRAINTS.md the set does not contain. Set B keeps the yahooquery cross-check, the 10-name reference check and an approval gate for the frontend-design direction. But it removes PPO agents from scope and rules out cloud compute, which contradicts the brief's rented GPU. Its brief is still framed around stage 1 only. Its M1 has no golden cases at all. Its interface tasks are serialized (T03 waits on T02), and T13–T15 wait on T12 for no code reason. It also has labelling defects (tasks titled 'spine' with Kind thicken; 'SSE' where the design uses WebSocket). Its ten milestones include a lopsided M5 that mixes app pages with the real-data run. Overall, A is the more complete and more buildable plan.
